title: Pro-étale descent, diamonds and small v-stacks, Part II: integral recovery and kimberlite specialization
summary: Extends DiamondsAndVStacks to formal and integral objects: diamondification forgets universal homeomorphisms and perfection; Gleason's reduction functor, formally adic maps, specializing v-sheaves, prekimberlites, kimberlites and formal and tubular neighbourhoods; recovery of flat normal formal and proper schemes over O_E from their v-sheaves (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 18.4.1, Lourenço's specialization-triple theorem, de Jong's theorem on power-bounded functions); v-closures; and Gleason's theorem that the specialization map of a topologically normal rich smelted kimberlite is a bijection on connected components.
readme:
This roadmap extends DiamondsAndVStacks from analytic adic spaces to formal and integral objects.
DiamondsAndVStacks constructs the integral pre-adic v-sheaf `X^♢` of an arbitrary pre-adic space
over `ℤ_p`, its Galois quotient and its point map, and proves seminormal full faithfulness on rigid
spaces over a fixed field; it stops there. This Part II starts at that point. It proves what
diamondification forgets (universal homeomorphisms and perfection), constructs Gleason's reduction
functor and specialization theory for v-sheaves that behave like formal schemes (prekimberlites,
kimberlites, formal and tubular neighbourhoods), recovers flat normal formal and proper schemes over
`O_E` from their v-sheaves (Scholze–Weinstein, Proposition 18.4.1), and proves Gleason's
connected-components theorem for topologically normal rich smelted kimberlites.

Sources: Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley lectures on p-adic geometry (Lectures 10 and 18); Gleason,
Specialization maps for Scholze's category of diamonds (arXiv:2012.05483v4); Anschütz–Gleason–
Lourenço–Richarz, On the p-adic theory of local models (arXiv:2201.01234v2, §2); Lourenço, The
Riemannian Hebbarkeitssätze for pseudorigid spaces (arXiv:1711.06903v1, §6); de Jong, Crystalline
Dieudonné module theory via formal and rigid geometry (Publ. IHÉS 82, §7); Kisin–Pappas–Zhou,
Integral models of Shimura varieties with parahoric level structure II (arXiv:2409.03689v3, §§3.1,
3.4); Gleason–Lim–Xu, The connected components of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties
(arXiv:2208.07195v3, §3).

Boundaries. Analytic and integral pre-adic diamondification, `Spd O_C/G_K = Spd O_K`, the point map
`|X^♢| → |X|` and seminormal rigid full faithfulness are DiamondsAndVStacks D6; the scheme v-topology
and perfect v-descent are ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.1 and AT.7; formal schemes, Huber's functor `t`,
Berthelot generic fibres and the classical specialization map are AdicSpacesPartII F0 and R2; partially
proper and proper maps of v-stacks are DiamondEtaleCohomology C4; Grothendieck existence is
AdicSpacesPartII F0. Local models, `B_dR^+`-Grassmannians, integral shtuka moduli and their kimberlite
structure are applications in GeometricSatakeAndFusion and HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas and their Part
IIs, which import this roadmap. The comparison with Ayoub's rigid analytic motives is not a target.
Reader document: research/blueprint/readmes/DiamondsAndVStacksPartII.md.

stages.title: What diamondification forgets: universal homeomorphisms and perfect schemes
stages.description:
## D7. What diamondification forgets: universal homeomorphisms and perfect schemes

Prove that diamondification sees only topology on the analytic side and only the perfection on
the characteristic-`p` side.

*Analytic invariance.* For a map `f : X → X'` of analytic pre-adic spaces over `Spa ℚ_p` that is a
universal homeomorphism and induces isomorphisms of completed residue fields, `O⁺_{X'}/p^n →
O⁺_X/p^n` is an isomorphism of sheaves on `|X| = |X'|` and `f^♦` is an isomorphism (Scholze–Weinstein,
Proposition 10.2.1 and Lemma 10.2.2). Prove the residue-field hypothesis for universal
homeomorphisms locally of finite type over a nonarchimedean field of characteristic `0`; the general
assertion is recorded as a gap.

*Perfect schemes.* For a scheme `X` over `𝔽_p` define `X^⋄` by gluing `Spd(A, A)` for discrete
affine charts, so `Spec(A)^⋄(Spa(R, R⁺)) = Hom(A, R⁺)`, and prove `X^⋄ = (X^perf)^⋄`, compatibility
with finite limits and open immersions, and the distinction from the analytic convention of
AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons. Prove the minimal-point lemma for quasicompact spaces over the
spectrum of a valuation ring and full faithfulness of `X ↦ X^⋄` on perfect schemes (Proposition
18.3.1, Lemma 18.3.2). Define Gleason's olivine spectrum `Spo(B, B⁺)` with the continuous bijection
`|Spd(B, B⁺)| → Spo(B, B⁺)`, a homeomorphism for formal pairs and pairs topologically of finite type
over a formal pair; describe schematic closed subsets; prove that a map of perfect affine schemes is
a v-cover exactly when its `⋄` is a surjection of v-sheaves; and prove Gleason's Theorem 2.32:
`Hom(Y, X) = Hom(Y^♢, X^♢)` for `Y` a perfect discrete adic space over `𝔽_p` and `X` any pre-adic
space over `ℤ_p`.

stages.title: Scheme-theoretic v-sheaves and the reduction functor
stages.description:
## D8. Scheme-theoretic v-sheaves and the reduction functor

Construct the category of small scheme-theoretic v-sheaves (sheaves on perfect affine
`𝔽_p`-schemes for the v-topology, through cutoff cardinals), their underlying topological spaces,
and the extension of `⋄` to them. Define the reduction functor `F ↦ F^red`,
`F^red(Spec R) = F(Spec(R)^⋄)`, as the right adjoint of `⋄` (Gleason, §3). Prove: perfect schemes are
reduced and `⋄` is fully faithful on reduced objects; `Spd(A, A⁺)^red = Spec(A_red)` with
`A_red = (A/A·A°°)^perf`, and reduction only sees the non-analytic locus; quasiseparated diamonds
have empty reduction.

Define formally adic maps (the reduction square is Cartesian), formally `p`-adic v-sheaves,
formally closed immersions and formally separated v-sheaves. Prove stability under composition and
base change; that a map of formal Huber pairs is adic exactly when its `Spd` is formally adic; that
a formally `p`-adic `Spd(A, A⁺)` comes from an adic map; that `Spd ℤ_p` is formally separated and the
diagonal of a formally `p`-adic v-sheaf is formally adic; the injectivity criterion for the
adjunction map; and that a formally closed subsheaf of `Spd(A)` has reduction `Spec(A/J)` for an open
ideal `J`. The examples `Spd(𝔽_p((t)), 𝔽_p[[t]]) → Spd 𝔽_p` (adic, not formally adic) and the
identity from the norm topology to the discrete topology (formally adic, not adic) are Checks.

stages.title: Specializing v-sheaves, prekimberlites and formal neighbourhoods
stages.description:
## D9. Specializing v-sheaves, prekimberlites and formal neighbourhoods

Define the specialization map `sp_A : |Spa(A, A⁺)| → |Spec(A⁺_red)|` of a Tate Huber pair, with
continuity, surjectivity, spectrality and closedness, and its bijectivity for strictly totally
disconnected spaces (Gleason, §4.1). Define formalizations, v-formalizing and v-locally formal
v-sheaves, and prove that a formally separated v-sheaf formalizes a map from an affinoid perfectoid
space in at most one way. Define specializing v-sheaves (formally separated and v-locally formal)
and construct the continuous, functorial specialization map `sp_F : |F| → |F^red|`.

Define prekimberlites (specializing, with `F^red` a scheme and `(F^red)^⋄ → F` a closed immersion)
and their analytic locus, and prove that separated locally noetherian formal schemes over `Spf ℤ_p`
give prekimberlites with reduction the perfection of `𝔛_red`. Define formal neighbourhoods
`F̂_{/S}` of locally closed subschemes `S ⊂ F^red`, with their base-change formula, their identification
with `Spd` of the completion for formal pairs, and openness for constructible `S`. Construct Heuer's
thickening `X^{⋄/◦}`, the specialization morphism `SP_F : F → (F^red)^{⋄/◦}` and the étale-formal
neighbourhoods `F ×_{(F^red)^{⋄/◦}} V^{⋄/◦}`; prove that reduction is an equivalence from
quasicompact formally adic étale prekimberlites over `F` to quasicompact separated étale perfect
schemes over `F^red` (Gleason, Theorem 4.27), and that formal schemes have formal-scheme étale
neighbourhoods.

stages.title: Integral models from their v-sheaves
stages.description:
## D10. Integral models from their v-sheaves

Recover flat normal formal schemes and proper flat normal schemes over `O_E` from their v-sheaves.
Here `E/ℚ_p` is complete and discretely valued with perfect residue field `k`.

*Inputs.* The two functors `X ↦ X^♢` and `X ↦ X^⋄` on `O_E`-schemes, with `X^⋄ → X^♢` a monomorphism
for separated `X`, an open immersion for separated `X` locally of finite type and an isomorphism for
proper `X` (Anschütz–Gleason–Lourenço–Richarz, Definition 2.10, Lemma 2.11). For `𝔛` locally
formally of finite type over `Spf O_E`: the Huber generic fibre `𝔛^ad ×_{Spa O_E} Spa(E, O_E)` is the
adic space of Berthelot's generic fibre, and `𝔛^♢ ×_{Spd O_E} Spd E` is its diamond; the generic
fibre of a flat normal `𝔛` is normal; de Jong's theorem `Γ(𝔛, O) = O°(𝔛_η)` for flat normal `𝔛`
(de Jong, Theorem 7.4.1; Lourenço, Corollary 6.3); the specialization map of `𝔛^♢` restricted to
classical points is Berthelot's; the analytic locus of `𝔛^♢` is the maximal open sub-v-sheaf that is
a diamond, with complement `(𝔛_red^perf)^⋄`; and the generic fibre is dense in `|𝔛^♢|` for flat `𝔛`.

*Closures.* A map of small v-sheaves is a closed immersion exactly when it is a quasicompact
monomorphism inducing a closed embedding on underlying spaces; a proper monomorphism is a closed
immersion. Define the v-closure of a sub-v-sheaf, prove that closed sub-v-sheaves correspond to
closed weakly generalizing subsets and that `|Y^cl|` is the weakly generalizing closure, and that
v-closures commute with open partially proper base change (AGLR §2.1).

*Targets.* The specialization-triple theorem: for `k` algebraically closed,
`𝔛 ↦ (𝔛_η, (𝔛_red)^perf, sp)` is fully faithful on flat normal formal schemes locally formally of
finite type (Scholze–Weinstein, Theorem 18.4.2, after Lourenço). Scholze–Weinstein Proposition
18.4.1: `𝔛 ↦ 𝔛^♢` is fully faithful from flat normal formal schemes locally formally of finite type
over `Spf O_E` to small v-sheaves over `Spd O_E`. Its scheme form: on proper flat normal `O_E`-schemes
`X ↦ X^♢` is fully faithful. The absolutely weakly normal variant (AGLR Theorem 2.16, Proposition
2.18). For a flat projective `O_E`-scheme that is the Zariski closure of its generic fibre in a proper
`P`, `X^♢` is the v-closure of `(X_E)^♢` in `P^♢`. Application: an integral model with a prescribed
v-sheaf, and a morphism with a prescribed map of v-sheaves, is unique (Kisin–Pappas–Zhou §3.1.9 and
Lemma 3.4.1).

stages.title: Kimberlites, tubular neighbourhoods and connected components
stages.description:
## D11. Kimberlites, tubular neighbourhoods and connected components

Define valuative prekimberlites (`SP_F` partially proper), with formal schemes and partially proper
maps as sources of examples and the specializing property of `sp_F`. Define smelted kimberlites
`(F, D)` (`D ⊂ F^an` open, a quasiseparated locally spatial diamond, `D → F` partially proper) and
kimberlites (`(F, F^an)` smelted with `sp_{F^an}` quasicompact); prove that separated locally
noetherian formal schemes give kimberlites. Define the tubular neighbourhood
`D^⊚_{/S} = F̂_{/S} ×_F D` of a constructible locally closed `S ⊂ |F^red|`, prove that it is a
smelted kimberlite and is the interior of `sp_D^{-1}(S)` (not the full fibre: a rank `> 1` point has
empty tube interior), and prove that `sp_D` is specializing and spectral, and closed for kimberlites.
Prove permanence under formally closed immersions and étale-formal neighbourhoods.

Define constructibly Jacobson diamonds (rank-one points dense in the constructible topology), with
permanence, Huber's density of classical points and diamonds with enough facets, and the density of
`D^⊚_{/S}` in `sp_D^{-1}(S)`. Define rich smelted kimberlites (valuative, `D` constructibly Jacobson,
`|F^red|` locally noetherian, `sp_D` surjective) and, separately, topologically normal rich pairs
(connected tubes at closed points). Prove Gleason's Lemma 4.53 (`sp_D` is a quotient map for a rich
pair), permanence of richness, and Lemma 4.55 (`π₀(sp_D) : π₀(|D|) → π₀(|F^red|)` is bijective for a
topologically normal rich pair). Define `π`-adic and flat `π`-adic kimberlites over `Spd O`, prove
flatness criteria through surjectivity of `sp`, the specialization-triple theorem for the category
`𝒦` of AGLR Definition 2.36, the properness criterion, and the normality criterion through connected
tubes (AGLR §2.3). Checks: a formal disc, a rank `> 1` valuation point with empty tube interior, a
pair that is not rich, and finite étale formal neighbourhoods.
